summary:
EarthBeat is a browser-based sonification prototype that turns NASA Earth visualization videos into an evolving soundscape. Users upload a visualization and watch it while EarthBeat analyzes each video frame in the browser using the HTML Canvas API, measuring average brightness, dominant RGB colors, and frame-to-frame visual changes.

These visual signals control procedural audio generated with the Web Audio API: brightness selects a note from a pentatonic scale, dominant color influences an in-scale harmony, and frame changes affect accents and note timing.

Using NASA's GEOS-FP Near-Surface Temperature visualization, EarthBeat explores another way to experience Earth-system patterns and aims to make visual science more accessible to blind and low-vision audiences. The generated sound is an artistic interpretation of pixel patterns, not a direct reading or measurement of temperature.
details:
EarthBeat — Hear Our Changing Planet

1. Project Overview

EarthBeat is an interactive browser-based application developed for NASA's Earth Information Jukebox challenge. It explores how scientific Earth visualizations can be transformed into sound, creating an alternative way for people to experience changes in our planet.

2. How It Works

  1. Users upload an Earth visualization video.
  2. EarthBeat displays and plays the uploaded video.
  3. The HTML Canvas API analyzes video frames in the browser.
  4. The application extracts average brightness, dominant RGB colors, and frame-to-frame visual differences.
  5. These visual characteristics control procedural audio generated using the Web Audio API.

3. Visual-to-Sound Mapping

  • Brightness selects a musical lead note from a pentatonic scale.
  • Dominant color influences the accompanying in-scale harmony.
  • Frame-to-frame changes influence sound accents and note timing.

This creates an evolving soundscape connected to the visual patterns in the uploaded video.

4. NASA Data

The prototype uses NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio resource, GEOS-FP Near-Surface Temperature (SVS 5147), credited to NASA's Global Modeling and Assimilation Office.

The project analyzes visual characteristics of the video. It does not independently retrieve or calculate actual temperature measurements. Its sound is an experimental interpretation of visual patterns, not a scientific temperature measurement or forecast.

5. Technology Stack

  • React
  • Vite
  • JavaScript
  • HTML Canvas API
  • Web Audio API
  • CSS

The application runs in the browser and processes uploaded media locally.

6. Creativity and Intended Impact

Earth science visualizations are commonly communicated through images, maps, and videos. EarthBeat explores an additional communication method by translating visual patterns into sound.

The project aims to make Earth science more engaging and explore alternative ways for blind and low-vision audiences to experience scientific visualizations. It can also support interactive learning for people interested in our changing planet.

7. Super Intelligence Assistance Disclosure

ChatGPT was used for brainstorming, technical guidance, and documentation assistance. OpenAI Codex was used to assist with code generation, implementation, and debugging.

The application uses procedural audio synthesis through the Web Audio API. No AI-generated music, images, or video were used in the project. The NASA visualization remains the original NASA-provided resource and is credited to NASA's Global Modeling and Assimilation Office.

The project is an experimental prototype, and its sonification should be understood as an interpretation of visual information rather than a replacement for scientific data or accessible scientific descriptions.
